It contains a rear position lamp (P-01, S-08) and a stop lamp (P-02, S-09), which match the definitions in R48|2.5.7 and R48|2.5.4. Both emit red light (P-01, P-02) through a red-tinted outer lens within the chromaticity limits (P-04, D-07), so they are red lamps under R48|2.11.1.4. No evidence suggests these functions are sidemarker lamps, so the exception does not apply. The requirement text's narrowing to the rear position and stop lamps is a consistent subset of the regulatory text. Applicability is established; whether the installed sight-lines actually comply is a separate compliance question to be resolved on the vehicle.

reason: R48|5.10.4.3 is the in-case-of-doubt verification method for R48|5.10.1, via its parent R48|5.10.4. R48|5.10.1 covers red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle, with 'lamp' defined in R48|2.1.5. The product is a rear lamp for an M1 vehicle (S-01, S-02). It contains red-emitting lamp functions: a rear position lamp emitting red light to the rear (P-01) and a stop lamp emitting red light to the rear (P-02), behind a red outer lens (P-04). The red-light-to-front scope is therefore met, so the provision applies when installed on the vehicle; whether the ≤0.25 cd limit is met is a compliance question. Two caveats do not change the decision. First, rear mounting is inferred from the product type (F-03) rather than stated as a vehicle installation position. Second, the extracted requirement covers only the red-to-front branch of the original 'and/or' text; the white-to-rear branch, which would concern the reversing lamp (P-03), is not part of this requirement. The test case's reference to 'Zone 1' is not supported by the supplied context, but this affects the test method, not applicability.

reason: Annex 9 1.1 (R48|Annex 9 1.1, under the 'Tests' parent R48|Annex 9 1) is a conformity-of-production check on installed lamp positions on production vehicles. Positions are verified with the vehicle unladen per R48|5.4, using the surface definitions in R48|2.10.2–2.10.4 and the vehicle edge in R48|2.3.3. The product is a rear lamp module (S-01) for an M1 passenger car (S-02). It combines the four lamp types named in the extracted requirement: rear position lamp (P-01, S-08), stop lamp (P-02, S-09), reversing lamp (P-03, S-10) and rear retro-reflector (P-05, S-12). These match the definitions in R48|2.5.7, 2.5.4, 2.5.12 and 2.5.8. So the subject matter is relevant. However, applicability cannot be confirmed for three reasons. (1) The product is a component, and the requirement is a vehicle-level installation check. There is no evidence that the product is assessed as installed on a production vehicle under an R48 vehicle approval; the rear-exterior mounting (F-03) is only inferred, and no vehicle installation data is given. (2) The original text says lamp position is 'as defined in paragraph 2.1.6.', but the supplied 2.1.6 (inside R48|2.1.5) defines 'Change index'. This is a reference discrepancy, already flagged as an unresolved reference. (3) The original text covers 'each lamp', while the extracted requirement narrows it to four functions. Its test case also cites paras 6.4, 6.7, 6.10 and 6.14, which are not in the supplied context. Because of these scope and extraction discrepancies, the result is unresolved.

reason: R48|5.10.1, under the general specifications (R48|5, R48|5.10) on light that could cause confusion, says red light from a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle shall not be visible from the front. Per R48|2.1.5, retro-reflectors also count as lamps. The extracted requirement names the rear position lamp, stop lamp and red retro-reflector. This is a subset of the source's 'a lamp fitted on the rear' scope, so it does not change applicability here. The product is a rear lamp module (S-01) for an M1 passenger car (S-02), covered by R48's M/N scope. It integrates a rear position lamp emitting red light to the rear (P-01, S-08), a stop lamp emitting red light to the rear (P-02, S-09, S-04) and a rear retro-reflector (P-05, S-12). A red-tinted outer lens defines the red colour (P-04, D-07), consistent with R48|2.11.1.4 and R48|2.11.2.4. Rear mounting is inferred from the product type and functions (F-03). Every function named in the requirement is present, so the requirement applies. Compliance is a separate question: whether red light is actually invisible from the front in the Zone 1 test depends on installed vehicle geometry, and nothing about that is evaluated here.

reason: The product is a rear lamp for an M1 vehicle (S-01, S-02, F-03). It emits red light from a rear position lamp and a stop lamp (P-01, P-02, P-04), so the subject matter of R48 5.10.1 is relevant: red light from a rear-fitted lamp must not be visible from the front (R48|5.10.1, R48|5.10.4). However, the extracted requirement does not faithfully reflect the original text. Paragraph 5.10.4.3 (R48|5.10.4.3) is a deemed-to-satisfy verification method for 5.10.1/5.10.2 that applies only 'in case of doubt'. It says the requirement is deemed fulfilled if intensity is ≤0.25 cd. The extracted text instead turns this into a mandatory 'shall not exceed 0.25 cd' limit. It also drops the alternative 'and/or white light emitted to the rear', which matters because the product includes a white reversing lamp (P-03). Because the requirement as stated misrepresents the regulatory obligation, applicability cannot be confirmed. A further unconfirmed point is the scope: R48 is an installation regulation, while the product is a lamp component. No product evidence gives forward red intensity or installation geometry.

These match the definitions in R48|2.5.7, R48|2.5.4 and R48|2.5.12 and are lamps under R48|2.1.5. They are therefore among the lamps whose connections and functioning this check covers. The narrowing of 'every lamp' to these three functions in the extracted requirement matches the product's content. The check is carried out on the production vehicle, and the vehicle wiring and tell-tale design determine whether the lamp complies, not whether the requirement applies. The 22 omitted passages and the absence of vehicle wiring details do not negate applicability.
